What the Garden Kept
Alt_Text: A terracotta pot filled with pink flowering blooms and layered green foliage rests on a pale cream surface against a deep violet background in a square original oil painting.
Tags: potted geraniums painting; floral still life original art; terracotta pot wall art; pink flowers painting; garden painting original; potted plant painting; impressionist floral painting; flower pot art; cottage garden painting; pink geraniums art; original oil painting; still life flower painting; garden still life art
Colors: Deep violet-purple; rose and dusty pink; warm terracotta and amber; yellow-green and deep forest green; cream and golden-warm white
Description: The background is a deep, settled violet — the kind that arrives when the afternoon starts to cool and the garden gets quiet. Against it, a terracotta pot holds a full cluster of pink blooms, loose and open, painted with the kind of gestural marks that suggest movement without wind. The light comes from low and to the side, warming the pot and the pale surface it rests on into amber and cream. The foliage layers between deep green and yellow-green, visible in quick, honest strokes that don't try to be more than they are. The painting holds one specific moment — the last of the warm before the evening arrives. Original oil painting. 8 × 8 inches. Sold framed and ready to hang. One of a kind.
Story: The pot sat in that last stretch of afternoon light, the kind that comes in low and warm right before the garden goes quiet.
Subject: Potted flowering plant — likely geraniums or a similar full-bloom variety — in a terracotta pot with saucer, resting on a pale ledge or surface.
Light_Description: Directional, warm, low light entering from the lower right. The pot and pale surface catch the warmth as amber and cream. The background is in deep shadow — saturated violet. The foliage reads against both the dark background and the warm light, creating a layered contrast. The light reads as late and specific.
